title: Remedies and Conflict of Laws
audience: a law student in a U.S. JD program
purpose: Analyze compensatory damages and their limits, restitution and unjust enrichment, injunctions and specific performance, equitable defenses, punitive damages and due process, declaratory relief and fees; then choice of law, recognition of judgments and constitutional limits on choice of law.

weeks.1: The goals of remedies and compensatory damages
weeks.2: Limits on damages: certainty, foreseeability and mitigation
weeks.9: Choice of law: the traditional vested-rights approach
weeks.10: Modern approaches: interest analysis and the Second Restatement
weeks.11: Recognition of judgments and full faith and credit
weeks.12: Constitutional limits on choice of law

blocks.deliverable: Compute damages for a breach with mitigation.
Choose between damages and restitution for a client.
Apply the four-factor test for a preliminary injunction.
Week 7 midterm; evaluate a punitive award under the due process guideposts.
Decide which law governs a multistate tort under two approaches.
Analyze whether a sister-state judgment must be enforced.
Submit the project; take an unseen 180 minute final in week 14.

project: Remedies strategy memo: for a supplied multistate dispute, decide which state's law applies, then recommend the best mix of remedies with damages computations, in 2,000 words.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
